title: The project that forgot itself
intro: Three months in, an SDD project has gone strangely sour: the agent keeps making 'obvious' mistakes it never used to make. Open the clues and diagnose.

facts.label: The specs
facts.value: requirements.md still describes the appointments table with a `therapist` column. The database has used `therapist_name` since a hotfix in week 3.

facts.label: Git history
facts.value: A dozen commits touch src/ only — quick manual patches with messages like 'fix css' and 'hotfix col name'. No spec files changed in any of them.

facts.label: The agent's behaviour
facts.value: It re-asks questions that were settled weeks ago, and its last feature contradicted two of those decisions.

facts.label: The team
facts.value: Reviews take longer every sprint — nobody can say what the system does without reading the code. One dev keeps a private notes file to cope.

facts.label: The constitution
facts.value: mission.md and tech-stack.md are intact and still accurate. The roadmap is up to date.

question: What went wrong with this project?
choices: The constitution was badly written from the start
Drift: hand-edited code desynced from the specs, so the specs now lie to the agent
The agent's model degraded and needs replacing
SDD doesn't work for projects older than a few weeks
debrief: Every clue points the same way: code changed in src/-only commits while requirements.md froze in week 3 — so the specs describe software that no longer exists. The agent isn't degrading; it's faithfully trusting documents that now lie, which is why it re-asks settled questions and contradicts old decisions. The private notes file is the giveaway symptom: **cognitive debt** is back, carried in one person's head. The cure is the rule that was skipped: route fixes **through the agent**, so spec and code move together — and when drift has already happened, run a replanning pass to resync before the next feature.
